text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A children's protest march in Tallinn on Sunday demanded more play-grounds in the centre of the city.

- Two Estonian entertainers, Erkki Kolu and Valdo Jahiloo, set a world record by telling anecdotes for 61 hours without a break in Tartu at the weekend; the former record of 60 hours was set in 1988 in Johannesburg.
- A hoard of 350 silver coins from the 17th century was uncovered by workers digging a ditch in Palamuse, central Estonia.
- A conflict broke out between the Estonia Opera soloists and the administration last week. The singers accuse the management of destroying the theatre.

- Three Baltic foreign ministers met in the island of Saaremaa on Sunday to discuss their NATO strategy. The ministers' position was that the first round of NATO enlargement should not be the last, officials said.
- Estonian athlete Erkki Nool finished fourth in a decathlon competition in Gotzis.
